queries.query: During the 28-day baseline, sleep averaged 465 min (start ~22:55, end fixed 07:00), steps ~7983, activity ~56 min, RHR 56.1 bpm, RMSSD 44.8 ms. In the 14-day window, sleep onset delayed sharply to ~00:47–01:05 with duration falling to a mean of 346 min (−118 min, range 335–355). Nighttime coverage dropped to 355–373 min from ~486 baseline. Steps (~8037), activity (~55 min), low movement, RHR (55.4 bpm), and RMSSD (44.9 ms) remained near baseline levels throughout.

During the 28-day baseline, sleep averaged 465 min with onset ~22:55 and offset fixed at 07:00. In the 14-day window, sleep onset delayed ~2 h to ~00:52, reducing duration by ~118 min to ~346 min; wake time remained 07:00. Steps (~7983 vs ~8037), activity (~56 vs ~55 min), low movement (~450 vs ~452 min), resting HR (~56.1 vs ~55.4 bpm), and RMSSD (~44.8 vs ~44.9 ms) were stable. Paired correlations were weak throughout. No missing data.

Over 28 baseline days, sleep averaged 465 min starting ~22:55 and ending exactly 07:00 daily, with steps ~7983, activity ~56 min, low movement ~450 min, RHR 56 bpm, and RMSSD 45 ms. In the 14-day window, sleep onset shifted abruptly to ~00:50 while wake time remained 07:00, reducing sleep by 118 min/day (mean 346 min) persistently without recovery. Steps (+54), activity (-1 min), low movement (+2 min), RHR (-0.8 bpm), and RMSSD (+0.2 ms) stayed near baseline. Evening activity intervals continued at 21:00; daytime low-movement blocks remained structured. Weekday/weekend patterns were stable. No meaningful activity-sleep or RHR-RMSSD correlations emerged in either period.

During your 28-day baseline you typically slept ~465 min (roughly 22:50–07:00). Over the past 14 days, sleep start shifted about two hours later to around 00:50 while wake time stayed fixed at 07:00, reducing recorded sleep to ~335–355 min (average ~346 min, down ~118 min). Nighttime device coverage also dropped from ~485 min to ~365 min, so some reduction may reflect shorter recording windows rather than sleep alone. Despite this, steps (~8037 vs ~7983), active minutes (~55), low movement, resting heart rate (~55 bpm), and HRV (~45 ms) all remained near baseline levels. The primary change is the later sleep onset and correspondingly shorter recorded sleep.

In the recent 14 days, your sleep pattern changed notably compared to your 28-day baseline. You started sleeping roughly two hours later (around 00:50 vs ~22:55), while still waking at 07:00, reducing your average sleep from about 7.7 to 5.8 hours. Despite this, your daily steps (~8,000), active minutes (~55), low-movement time, resting heart rate (~55-56 bpm), and HRV (~45 ms) all stayed very close to baseline levels. The shorter sleep window is the main observed difference; daytime activity and heart metrics remained consistent.

Your sleep start shifted ~2 hours later in the recent 14 days (from ~22:55 to ~00:50), while wake time stayed at 07:00, reducing average sleep from ~465 to ~346 min. Steps (~8000), active minutes (~55), resting HR (~55-56 bpm) and RMSSD (~45 ms) remained near baseline. The shorter sleep reflects delayed onset rather than earlier waking.

During the 28-day baseline, steps averaged ~8009 per day with sleep ~470 min (start ~22:50, end 07:00), activity ~55 min, low movement ~451 min, resting heart rate 55-57 bpm, and HRV RMSSD 43-47 ms. In the 14-day window, steps declined sharply to a mean of ~2335 per day, roughly one-third of baseline. Sleep timing, duration, activity duration, low movement, RHR, and HRV remained stable and near baseline levels throughout. No other metric changed meaningfully alongside the step decrease. Wear compliance was complete across all 42 days.

Across 28 days baseline and 14 days window, sleep (~470 min, ending exactly 07:00 daily), activity (~55 min), low movement (~451 min), resting heart rate (~56 bpm), and HRV RMSSD (~45 ms) remained stable. Steps dropped abruptly from a baseline mean of 8009 to a window mean of 2335, persisting throughout all 14 window days without recovery. Despite this ~71% reduction in steps, activity duration was unchanged, indicating the step decrease did not correspond to reduced active minutes. Evening activity intervals continued daily ~21:00. No meaningful weekday/weekend patterns or cross-metric correlations emerged.

During the 28-day baseline, daily steps averaged ~8009 with stable sleep (~470 min, 22:50–07:00), activity (~55 min), low movement (~451 min), RHR (~56 bpm), and RMSSD (~45 ms). In the 14-day window, steps dropped abruptly to a mean of ~2335 (range 2064–2636), a 71% decrease persisting throughout. All other metrics remained near baseline levels: sleep ~470 min, activity ~55 min, low movement ~453 min, RHR ~56 bpm, RMSSD ~45 ms. No gradual transition preceded the step reduction.

Your 28-day baseline showed ~8,009 steps/day, sleep averaging ~470 min (starting ~22:50, ending 07:00), active minutes ~55, RHR ~55.7 bpm, and RMSSD ~45 ms, all with low day-to-day variability. In the 14-day window, steps dropped markedly to ~2,335/day (−71%), while sleep duration, timing, active minutes, low-movement minutes, RHR, and RMSSD remained essentially unchanged. No strong correlation between steps and active minutes or sleep appeared in either period. The step reduction is isolated to that metric; other recorded patterns are stable. Consider whether device wear location or step-detection conditions changed during the window.

Over the past 14 days, your sleep, activity duration (~55 min/day), resting heart rate (~56 bpm), HRV (~45 ms), and low movement remained very close to your 28-day baseline. Sleep averaged ~470 min, consistently ending at 07:00. The major change is in steps: they dropped from a baseline average of ~8,009/day to ~2,335/day, a ~71% decrease sustained across all 14 days, affecting weekdays and weekends alike. Despite this large reduction in recorded steps, your active minutes did not change, suggesting step counting conditions changed while overall active time was maintained. Other metrics showed no corresponding shift.

Sleep, active minutes (~55), resting HR (~56 bpm), and RMSSD (~45 ms) in your 14-day window remained very close to your 28-day baseline, with sleep consistently ending at 07:00. However, recorded steps dropped sharply from ~8,009 to ~2,335 per day. Because device wear time and all other metrics were unchanged, this likely reflects a change in step detection or how the device was worn rather than an actual activity change. Consider checking device placement.
